description: A transfer student with a background in systems programming who excels at implementation and debugging but feels less certain about the formal mathematical proofs required for algorithmic analysis.

nodes.description: A deep dive into C++ classes, inheritance, and manual memory management through the lens of the Goodrich textbook.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with strong_prior_exposure, the core focus remains on aligning prior knowledge with the specific C++ standards used in this course.
nodes.title: Advanced C++ Foundations & OOD

nodes.description: Exploring template metaprogramming, move semantics, and RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) to optimize data structure performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong_prior_exposure, enrichment nodes on advanced memory management are provided in place of basic scaffolding.
nodes.title: C++ Performance Optimization & Templates

nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core concepts for recursion and linear data structures required for all students regardless of strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Implementing singly and doubly linked lists and applying recursive thinking to linear structures.
nodes.title: Linked Lists & Recursion Principles

nodes.description: Formal assessment on recursion implementation and asymptotic Big-O analysis of list operations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standardized assessment (Quiz 1) to ensure the student with strong_prior_exposure meets the core competency benchmarks.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Analysis

nodes.personalizationRationale: Foundational sequence structures required for cumulative learning, built upon the student's strong_prior_exposure to programming.
nodes.description: Standard implementations of Stacks and Queues using both arrays and linked lists.
nodes.title: Stacks & Queues Implementation
Vectors & Iterator Patterns
nodes.description: Exploring C++ STL-style vectors, iterators, and the mechanics of dynamic array resizing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core material on iterators which is essential for understanding how C++ interacts with data sequences.
Standard curriculum content on sorting complexity that forms the basis for midterm evaluations.
nodes.description: Analysis of sequence-based sorting algorithms like Bubble Sort and their performance implications.
nodes.title: Sequences & Bubble Sort Analysis

nodes.personalizationRationale: The midterm review checkpoint ensures the student with strong_prior_exposure is prepared for the first major exam.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of material from blocks 1-3 and formal Quiz 2 assessment.
nodes.title: Midterm Review & Quiz 2

nodes.description: Structural properties of general trees and implementation of depth-first and breadth-first search traversals.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core tree theory required for all students to progress toward balanced search trees.
nodes.title: Tree Structures & Traversals

nodes.description: Specialized binary tree properties, including complete and full binary trees in C++.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential binary tree foundations required for the subsequent study of heaps and search trees.
nodes.title: Binary Tree Implementations

nodes.description: The heap data structure as a realization of a priority queue, focusing on the heap-order property.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for block 05, scaling the node count to match the smaller syllabus block size.
nodes.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
Maps & Hash Tables
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core content for block 06, framing hashing within the context of efficient dictionary ADTs.
nodes.description: Design and implementation of hash functions, collision resolution, and skip list structures.

nodes.title: Quiz 3: Hashing & Maps
nodes.description: Assessment on the efficiency of various hashing strategies and skip list operations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Quiz 3 provides a necessary checkpoint for map-based structures before moving to complex trees.

nodes.title: BSTs & AVL Trees
nodes.description: Binary Search Tree (BST) mechanics and the maintenance of the AVL balance property.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for the most theory-heavy block; student's strong_prior_exposure aids in grasping these complex proofs.

nodes.title: Multi-Way Search & Red-Black Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: Completes the core requirement for block 07 by covering advanced balanced search tree variants.
nodes.description: Exploring (2,4) trees and their relationship to Red-Black tree properties and rotations.

nodes.title: Advanced Sorting Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core sorting content required for the capstone block of the course.
nodes.description: Efficient O(n log n) sorting algorithms including Merge Sort and Selection Sort comparisons.
Final assessment on sorting algorithms and specialized data structure topics.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Quiz 4 ensures mastery of the final technical block before the cumulative review.
nodes.title: Quiz 4: Sorting & Topics
Final Cumulative Review Checkpoint
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory final-exam review checkpoint as per the course cumulative requirement for students of all tiers including strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: A comprehensive review of the entire syllabus, focused on exam preparation and cumulative logic.
